instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.

MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each); very short answers carry 2 marks (30–50 words); short answers 3 marks (50–80 words); long answers 5 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: (a) What is the van't Hoff factor of K2SO4? (b) Write the expression for the elevation of boiling point of an electrolyte using it.
State true or false: (a) An isolated system exchanges neither energy nor matter. (b) The enthalpy of formation of an element in its standard state is unity.
Write the K_sp expression for (a) AgCl (b) CaF2.
Fill in: (a) At the anode ______ takes place. (b) The EMF of the cell Zn | Zn^2+ || Cu^2+ | Cu with E°Zn = −0.76 V and E°Cu = +0.34 V is ______.
Match: (a) Quicklime (b) Gypsum (c) Washing soda with (i) Na2CO3·10H2O (ii) CaO (iii) CaSO4·2H2O.
Give (a) the oxidation states of nitrogen in NH3 and HNO3 and (b) a pair of elements showing the inert pair effect.
questions.answer: (a) −3 and +5. (b) Tl (+1 more stable than +3) and Pb (+2 more stable than +4).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is a basic buffer? Give an example and explain how it works.
questions.answer: A solution of a weak base and its salt with a strong acid (NH4OH + NH4Cl). On adding acid, OH− of the base neutralises it; on adding base, NH4+ neutralises OH−, so the pH changes little.

questions.q: Why is the use of a salt bridge necessary in a galvanic cell?
questions.answer: It completes the internal circuit by allowing ions to flow, maintains electrical neutrality in the half cells and avoids liquid junction potential, so the current continues.

questions.q: Why are the alkali metals kept in kerosene oil?
questions.answer: They are highly reactive and react vigorously with moisture and oxygen of air; kerosene prevents this contact.

questions.q: Why do the p-block elements show variable oxidation states?
questions.answer: They have both ns and np electrons available; the np electrons are lost or shared first, followed by the ns pair, giving states that differ by two (e.g. +3 and +5 in P).

questions.q: Why are noble gases chemically inert?
questions.answer: They have completely filled valence shells (ns² np⁶), very high ionisation enthalpies and positive electron gain enthalpies.

questions.q: Why is Zn not considered a transition element?
questions.answer: Zn^2+ has a completely filled d¹⁰ subshell; it has no incomplete d subshell in its atom or its common ion.

questions.q: Name the complex [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 and state its coordination number.
What is heterolytic fission? What are the species formed?
questions.answer: Cleavage of a covalent bond in which the shared pair goes to one atom, forming a cation and an anion (carbocation or carbanion). They initiate reactions as electrophiles or nucleophiles.

questions.q: Describe the ozonolysis of ethene with equations.
questions.answer: CH2=CH2 + O3 → ozonide; ozonide + Zn/H2O → 2HCHO + ZnO (two molecules of methanal).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the oxidising and dehydrating properties of concentrated sulphuric acid with examples.
questions.answer: Oxidising: Cu + 2H2SO4 → CuSO4 + SO2 + 2H2O; C + 2H2SO4 → CO2 + 2SO2 + 2H2O. Dehydrating: it removes water from blue vitriol (CuSO4·5H2O → white CuSO4) and chars sugar (C12H22O11 → 12C + 11H2O).

questions.q: Explain the inductive effect and its effect on the acidity of carboxylic acids.
questions.answer: The permanent polarisation of a σ bond by an electronegative group; –I groups such as Cl stabilise the carboxylate and increase the acidity (ClCH2COOH is stronger than CH3COOH), while +I groups (alkyl) decrease it (HCOOH is stronger than CH3COOH).

questions.q: Write the product when diethyl ether reacts with (a) HI (excess) (b) HI (1 mol), and give reasons for the stability of ethers to bases.
questions.answer: (a) C2H5OC2H5 + 2HI → 2C2H5I + H2O. (b) C2H5OC2H5 + HI → C2H5I + C2H5OH. Ethers are stable to bases and reducing agents because the C–O bond is strong and has no acidic hydrogen.

questions.q: Explain why amino acids behave as amphoteric substances and exist as zwitterions.
questions.answer: They have an acidic –COOH and a basic –NH2; in solution the proton transfers from –COOH to –NH2 giving the dipolar ion H3N+–CHR–COO−, which can react with both acids and bases.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) Discuss the halogenation of alkanes: mechanism and reactivity. (b) Write the products of monochlorination of propane.
questions.answer:
(a) A free-radical chain reaction: initiation by sunlight forming Cl•; propagation by H abstraction and attack on Cl2; termination by radical coupling. The reactivity order of H is 3° > 2° > 1° and of halogens F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2.
(b) CH3CH2CH3 + Cl2 → CH3CH2CH2Cl (1-chloropropane) + CH3CHClCH3 (2-chloropropane) + HCl.

questions.q: (a) What is aldol condensation? Write the mechanism for ethanal. (b) State the conditions for the Cannizzaro reaction and compare it with aldol condensation.
questions.answer:
(a) Aldehydes or ketones having α-hydrogen condense in dilute base to give β-hydroxy carbonyl compounds. Mechanism: OH− removes an α-H from CH3CHO to give the enolate −CH2CHO, which attacks the carbonyl carbon of another CH3CHO, forming CH3CH(O−)CH2CHO; protonation gives 3-hydroxybutanal, which dehydrates on heating to but-2-enal.
(b) Cannizzaro: aldehydes without α-hydrogen (HCHO, C6H5CHO) with conc. NaOH – one molecule is oxidised to carboxylate and the other reduced to alcohol. Aldol needs α-hydrogen and dilute alkali.
